newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH OPPOSITION LINKS FLOOD RELIEF TO REFORMS.
newsitem.headline: POLISH OPPOSITION LINKS FLOOD RELIEF TO REFORMS.

text.p: Poland's influential opposition party, the Union for Freedom (UW), on Sunday said the reconstruction of flood-hit areas should be accompanied by needed reforms, PAP news agency reported.

"There is no miracle plan to rebuild flooded lands, authentic reforms of the economy and the system of government must accompany reconstruction," PAP quoted UW leader Leszek Balcerowicz, a former finance minister, as saying.

The UW said that more power and funds should be given to provincial authorities in order to make the huge reconstruction effort run smoother and that Poland's present ruling coalition was not doing enough to decentralise the country's bureaucracy.

The centre-right UW has between 6 and 13 percent public support in opinion polls ahead of parliamentary elections on September 21, but remains among the favorites to become a smaller partner in a number of possible ruling coalitions.

Balcerowicz said the introduction of a flood tax should be a last resort and that the government should better manage existing resources and seek additional funds for reconstruction through foreign aid and privatisation.

Balcerowicz, the architect of Poland's "shock-therapy" economic transformation in the early 1990's, also said that the tax burden on firms should be decreased and that reconstruction credits should be available for small and mid-sized firms.
